newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Convicted murderer is retried for Brazil massacre.
newsitem.headline: Convicted murderer is retried for Brazil massacre.

text.p: A former policeman who was convicted of murder for his self-confessed role in a shooting spree in which eight street children died four years ago, pleaded innocent at his retrial on Wednesday, a court official said.
Nelson Oliveira dos Santos Cunha, 29, was sentenced to 261 years in jail in November last year on eight charges of murder and one of attempted murder.
Under Brazilian law anyone sentenced to more than 20 years in jail for a crime has the automatic right to a retrial.

Six children were killed when men indiscriminately opened fire on about 70 children playing or sleeping on the steps of the Candelaria Church in downtown Rio early on July 23, 1993. Two others had been killed earlier and left nearby, and six children were injured in the shooting spree.

Cunha, a recent born-again Christian, who resigned from the Rio police force after the massacre, voluntarily confessed his role in the killings to police in April last year, just days before the first of five men accused of the massacre, Marcus Vinicius Borges Emmanuel, went on trial.
At his first trial, Cunha testified that he, Emmanuel and two other police officers, one of whom has since been murdered and one who is awaiting trial, committed the killings.

In his testimony, he blamed the police officer who has since been murdered, for most of the killings, but admitted to having accidentally shot and wounded one of the victims of the massacre, Wagner dos Santos, who is also a key witness in the Candelaria trials.
Cunha's testimony helped three other men accused of the massacre to be declared innocent, despite declarations by Wagner dos Santos who identified one of the three men as one of the killers.
Cunha is expected to achieve a reduction in his jail sentence, as did Emmanuel, who was sentenced to 309 years and had his sentence reduced by 220 years at his retrial.
